teaser: One vague prompt can't redesign onboarding, so Maya splits it into three focused deliverables and learns how far to chop and how to hand off.

scene.title: This request is too big for one prompt
scene.sceneHtml:
Maya's story: Week 3 – "This request is too big for one prompt"

Maya's manager asked her to "Redesign the new-hire onboarding process." Maya typed that into Claude. Claude gave a vague 3-paragraph overview. She tried again with more detail — the output was slightly better but still shallow.

Her colleague said, "That request has three distinct deliverables: a process map, supporting training materials, and a measurement plan. Break it into three focused prompts; each one will be stronger than trying to do all three at once." Maya decomposed the task. Each prompt produced a specific, well-structured deliverable. She combined them into a final proposal.

takeaways: Decompose when a request needs multiple distinct deliverables (map + materials + plan); one complex deliverable still gets a single prompt.
Over-decomposition reads fragmented and choppy; the fix is to consolidate related steps into fewer cohesive sections, not add headings.
A reliable human-in-the-loop hand-off documents both what Claude must produce and the exact criteria the reviewer checks before approval.
Improve recurring workflows structurally: move repeated reference material into a Project and add a quality gate before downstream use.
